title: pen-sync.config.json
description: Where the pen-sync scripts find a repo's component package, registry, Storybook, tokens and Pencil file, and how its themes switch. Every key is optional; `init.mjs` writes a starting file.

package.description: The component package, relative to the repo root.

packageName.description: The package's import name, so `@scope/pkg/…` imports count toward a component's source hash.

registry.description: The design-system registry (ids, levels, files), relative to `package`.

variants.description: The generated variant axes, relative to `package`.

storybook.description: The running Storybook the exports render.

playwright.description: A package.json, relative to the repo root, whose dependencies include `playwright`.

pen.description: The Pencil design-system file, relative to the repo root.

library.description: The library reference `pen-library.mjs` writes for agents designing in Pencil, relative to the repo root.

tokens.description: The resolved design tokens (DTCG JSON) `export-tokens.mjs` writes, relative to the repo root.

tokenSource.description: The token stylesheet the token export resolves per theme, relative to `package`.

typographyClass.description: The class that applies one typography role (a `--type-<role>-size` set in `tokenSource`), with `{role}` for its name. A Tailwind `@utility` counts as a class.

docgen.description: A module, relative to the repo root, exporting `createDocgenSession({ cwd })` that `variants.mjs` reads prop types through. Null uses the bundled one, on the repo's TypeScript 5 or 6 (`PEN_SYNC_TYPESCRIPT` points at another install).

source.description: Commands that stand in for Storybook and Chromium, for components that don't render in a browser. Each runs from the repo root without a shell and writes to its `{out}`. Null renders stories.

snapshot.description: Writes one component under one theme to `{out}` as JSON: `{ instances: [{ key, row, tree }], matrix: { rows, slots }, surfaces }`, trees as `snapshotMatrix` records them. Holes: {id} {theme} {out}.

tokens.description: Writes one theme's resolved tokens to `{out}` as JSON: `{ tokens: { name: { type, value } }, typography }`. Holes: {theme} {out}.

shots.description: Writes one 2x PNG per variant into the folder `{out}`, and `storybook.json` listing them, for pen-polish. Holes: {id} {theme} {out}.

boards.description: The boards `init.mjs` creates, instead of one per atomic level.

levels.description: `[level, title]` pairs. A registry entry's `level` and a `pen-import` entry's choose among them.

polishDir.description: Where polish passes write their PNGs.

penCommand.description: The pen.dev CLI command (`PEN_SYNC_PEN` overrides it, e.g. `bunx @pen.dev/cli@0.3.14` in CI).

usage.description: Folders, relative to the repo root, `variant-usage.mjs` counts variant uses in.

metadataPrefix.description: The `metadata.type` on the nodes the sync writes: `<prefix>` on components, `<prefix>-section` on sections, `<prefix>-slot` on level boards. Never change it on an existing file.

aliasOrder.description: Regex sources for token families, tried in order when a paint matches several tokens and no class names one. Semantic surfaces first, special-purpose families last.

chrome.description: The variables a component's section card in Pencil is drawn with.

brand.description: The fill of a matrix row with `surface: "brand"`.

themes.description: Every theme the tokens resolve under; the first is the default. Each is one Pencil theme (a value per axis), how Storybook renders a story in it, and how <html> switches the token CSS to it.

key.description: The theme's name in the tokens file and polish output, e.g. `dark` or `dark/brand-b`.

pencil.description: Its Pencil theme: one value per theme axis, e.g. `{ "mode": "dark" }`. Every theme sets the same axes.

storybook.description: The Storybook globals that render a story in it (`?globals=theme:dark`). Null for a theme only the tokens have.

html.description: Attributes on <html> that switch the token CSS to it (`{ "class": "dark" }`). Also how an export tells the theme has applied.
